Independent exact rational replay using A=diag(2,1), B with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal 1/2, gamma=3/4, sigma=1/8 and theta=0,1/2,1,3/2,2, and scalar rejection for theta=−1/2,5/2 using gamma=1/2 and sigma=37/100
correctness.rationale: With P=(I+gamma B)^(-1) and u=P(z−gamma b), the prox equation gives (z−u)/gamma=Bu+b, so the source normal residual is Hu+a+b with invertible Jacobian HP, in that order even for noncommuting A,B. Its Newton direction is exactly z_*−z, for z_*=(I+gamma B)x_*+gamma b. At the full trial, affine prox yields x_*+(1−theta)(y−x_*); quadratic energy above the minimum is therefore (1−theta)^2 times that at y. To check the decrease independently, put d=y−hat x. Quadratic Taylor identities and proximal optimality give phi(y)−phi(hat x)=−||d||^2/gamma+d^T(A−B)d/2, at most −gamma(2−gamma L_f)||R_nat(hat x)||^2/2. Thus every theta in [0,2] passes, strictly at nonstationarity because sigma is below that coefficient; theta=1 lands at x_*. No invertibility of the forward map is needed. For any fixed theta outside the interval, choose the scalar L=1, g=0, gamma=1/2, hat x nonzero. Acceptance requires (1−theta)^2/4<=1−2sigma. The admissible upper limit sigma=3/8 is excluded, but the right side tends down to 1/4 there, proving existence of a rejecting admissible sigma for each such theta. This is universal sharpness over the legal parameters, not a claim about every fixed sigma.
residual_risks: The legal interval is strictly 0<gamma<2/L_f, with no claim at its excluded upper endpoint. The finite replay does not establish the universal claim; no formal verification is credited.
The direction must be exact normal Newton up to scalar; a generic quasi-Newton direction is not covered.

originality.rationale: The defining paper supplies a decrease test and eventual superlinear-step result, not this global characterization of relaxed exact normal Newton on quadratics. Newton solving an affine residual by itself is standard. The supported distinction is universal acceptance for every admissible decrease parameter, including the part of the stepsize range at and above 1/L_f, together with the matching failure outside the relaxation interval. The closest inspected independent normal-map Newton algorithm uses a different merit and only an eventual unit-step guarantee.
residual_risks: Bounded comparisons cannot exclude another explicit quadratic specialization. The Zeng et al. published server did not yield a readable PDF; the identified lawful preprint was read, so any published-version differences are unassessed.

value.rationale: The result determines a sharp safeguard boundary for a named algorithm. In particular it gives full acceptance even in the doubled stepsize range outside the faster local theorem's hypotheses, and includes the reflection that leaves proximal-gradient energy unchanged. The simple scalar obstructions distinguish an exact universal interval from just another sufficient estimate.
residual_risks: Does not bound the cost of forming the exact direction, predict arbitrary approximate Newton acceptance or extend the general local convergence theorem beyond its stated range.
